solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One's drunk by saucer-sips — sign of progressive senility

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy from sipping out of saucers, which is itself a sign of growing old and dotty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's drunk' reads as a person who is drunk; the anagram signal is 'drunk', working on BY plus SAUCER-SIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Presbyacusis is the gradual hearing loss that comes with old age, a typical symptom of ageing.

clue.text: Glandular infection, one seen in top artists, ailing

indicators.note: ailing means unwell, out of sorts, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical note that leading painters, unwell, suffer from a gland infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' only tells you the I joins the letters of TOP ARTISTS before 'ailing' scrambles them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostatitis is inflammation of the prostate, a gland in men, often caused by infection.

clue.text: Short-story writer, after taking year out, carried over

indicators.note: after taking leads into removing something from the writer's name
out completes the instruction that the year is taken out of the name

parts.note: Damon Runyon, the American writer of Broadway short stories

explanation.surface: An author's work, edited a year later, carried over to the next page.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon Runyon wrote the Guys and Dolls stories; 'after taking' ... 'out' removes the Y from RUNYON.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-on describes text or a line that is continued without a break onto the next, i.e. carried over.

clue.text: Cars out of order — lubricate one on account (joint)

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters of cars are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to oil something is to lubricate it
one is the Roman numeral I
AC is short for account, the a/c of banking

explanation.surface: Instructions for a garage: the cars are broken, so oil one and put it on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' turns CARS into SACR. The bracketed 'joint' looks like an aside but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacroiliac is the joint between the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis.

clue.text: Twitcher, half dead, in grip of stress

indicators.note: in grip of means held inside, so one part is gripped by the other

parts.note: birr is a Scots word for force or emphasis, hence stress
the first half of the word dead

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher, worn out and half dead, suffering from stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Birr, an old Scots word for force or vigour, is in Chambers; 'in grip of' means the half of dead sits between its two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitcher is British slang for a keen birdwatcher who chases rare sightings, the same as a birder.

clue.text: Surrendered garland swept up in swirling eddy

indicators.note: in tells you the reversed garland sits inside the swirled letters
swirling means whirling about, so the letters of eddy are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: swept up in a down entry means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: A flower garland was carried off by a whirlpool and lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or hand over, so yielded is a synonym for surrendered.

clue.text: RC recitation, mean if shortened?

definitions.meaning: first sense: the ... (... Maria) is a Roman Catholic prayer recited with the rosary
second sense: a short form of average, which is the mean

explanation.walkthrough: RC is Roman Catholic; the question mark admits that the second sense is an abbreviation rather than a full word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary prayer is called the Ave, and ave. is a common contraction of average, another name for the mean.

clue.text: Last pair quitting bridge for the other side

indicators.note: the final two letters of the word for bridge leave it

parts.note: contract bridge is the full name of the card game

explanation.surface: A bridge player abandons the last partnership and goes over to the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' gives CONTRACT, the usual form of the card game; 'Last pair quitting' takes off its final CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin for against, used in English for the opposing case or the other side of an argument.

clue.text: Drunk amid mounting litter? Divorce results

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one part goes inside the other
mounting in a down entry means climbing, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals such as pups
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy owner among a pile of puppies, with the marriage breaking down as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: A split-up is a separation or breakup of a couple, which is what a divorce amounts to.

clue.text: Blob held in palm, a smidgen

indicators.note: held in means contained, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: the ita is the miriti palm of South America
O is a round blob, as in nought

explanation.surface: A tiny drop held in the hollow of someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palm' is the tree, not the hand: ITA is a Chambers palm, and 'held in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a very small amount, the Greek letter used for the least bit, so a synonym for smidgen.

clue.text: Persian verse in modiÞed rhythm, not to Þrst person

indicators.note: not means the following word to is dropped in favour of the person

parts.note: rubato is the musical freedom of varying the tempo
taken as written
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: Poetry read in a loose rhythm and not addressed to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to first person' means drop TO, leaving RUBA, and put I in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubai is a Persian quatrain, the form of the stanzas in the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.

clue.text: Public opinion (6, two words)

parts.note: a plain description of the Latin phrase for the voice of the people, given without wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition clue: Azed prints only the definition and readers send in their own cryptic clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pop, from vox populi, the voice of the people, means the views of the public, often gathered in street interviews.

clue.text: Author with little to do and year left, having standard quota on hand

parts.note: to pen is to write, so pen stands for author
a tad is a little bit
to act is to do

explanation.surface: A writer with little to do and a year left has a quota to work through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' is literal: the normal quota of fingers on a hand is five.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentadactyl means having five digits on each limb, the standard number of fingers on a hand.

clue.text: Corn seen waving, like a TV picture

indicators.note: corn waving in the wind is moving about, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A field of corn swaying in the breeze, as pretty as a picture on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on screen is displayed on a television or film screen, as a TV picture is.

clue.text: Circus performer behaving hilariously with applause around

indicators.note: around means the applause surrounds the other part

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of applause
ariot is a Chambers adverb meaning riotously, being a riot

explanation.surface: A clown at the circus fooling about to the sound of clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The circus here is the Roman arena for chariot races, not a big top; 'with ... around' wraps the applause about the riotous part.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a chariot in races in the Roman circus, the arena for such contests.

clue.text: Cocktail, taste lacking a dash of vermouth

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to savour is to taste and enjoy
the first letter of vermouth

explanation.surface: A cocktail that tastes wrong because the barman forgot the splash of vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes A and V from SAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour is a cocktail of spirit with lemon or lime juice, such as a whisky sour.

clue.text: Scottish region that has group almost open-mouthed

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: hiant is a Chambers word for gaping

explanation.surface: A part of Scotland whose people gape in amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiant, gaping, is a rare Chambers word; 'almost' trims it to HIAN. Lothian is the area around Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothian is a historic region of south-east Scotland that includes Edinburgh.

clue.text: Roman auxiliaries enemy rated unstable if reduced by half

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: unstable means shaky, not fixed, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
keep only the first half of the word if

explanation.surface: Roman allied troops judged the enemy shaky once it was halved in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' turns RATED into DERAT; halving IF leaves I.
explanation.definitionFit: Foederati were tribes bound to Rome by treaty to supply soldiers as auxiliary troops.

clue.text: One millions held in dreadful esteem

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: held in means contained, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: dire means dreadful
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Someone with millions is held in awful regard.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, a verb synonym of esteem.

clue.text: Irish traveller turned up, a bit drunk, in old-fashioned helmet

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany gypsy, a traveller
on is slang for slightly tipsy

explanation.surface: An Irish wanderer arrives tipsy, wearing an antique helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses IRROM to MORRI; 'turned up' reads like 'arrived', which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A morion (also morrion) is a 16th-century open helmet with a crest and curved brim.

clue.text: Arboreal primate waggling its rear

indicators.note: waggling means shaking about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling monkey wiggling its backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsier is a small big-eyed primate of South-East Asian forests that lives in trees.

clue.text: What's left by plough, acre for plant genus

parts.note: a rut is a furrow or track left in the ground

explanation.surface: A furrow cut by the plough across an acre where a plant grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruta is the botanical genus of rue, a bitter strong-smelling herb.

clue.text: Hammer or punch idiot?

definitions.meaning: first sense: both are examples of an implement
second sense: a slang word for a stupid or contemptible person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' and 'punch' look like verbs about assault; they are nouns, examples of hand implements.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammer and a punch are both workshop implements, and the same word is slang for a fool.

clue.text: Script in which old menial is sent up for periods

indicators.note: in which means the script holds the other part inside it

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script

indicators.note: sent up in a down entry means read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: an esne was an Anglo-Saxon labourer of the lowest class

explanation.surface: A manuscript in which an old servant is mocked over periods of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The esne, an Anglo-Saxon serf, is a crossword stalwart; 'sent up' gives ENSE, which 'in which' puts inside the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Menses is the medical term for menstrual flow, a woman's monthly periods.

clue.text: Bat, maybe amateur having work-out, caught by cover

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the other part

parts.note: a lid is a cover
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A cricket bat used by an amateur who exercises and is caught in the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' is the animal, not cricket gear, and 'cover' is a lid rather than the fielding position; 'caught by' makes LIPED.
explanation.definitionFit: An aliped is an animal with winged feet, with membranes joining its toes, which a bat is.

clue.text: Take care of house that's all right inside (6, two words)

indicators.note: inside places the second part within the first

parts.note: house is the British game of chance also called lotto or loto
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Look after a home that is fine inside.
explanation.walkthrough: House is an old British name for bingo, also called lotto or loto; 'inside' puts OK within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To look to something is to attend to it or tend it, which means taking care of it.

clue.text: Pipe from river: I go wrong, hiding it in trunk abroad

indicators.note: hiding it in means the preceding pieces are tucked inside the next word

parts.note: the American trunk of a car is the British boot
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A pipe recovered from a river, damaged and stowed in a car trunk overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The British boot of a car is the American trunk, hence 'trunk abroad'. 'hiding it in' puts RIERR after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier root pipe is a tobacco pipe carved from the root of the briar heath, so the word names the pipe.

clue.text: Treated this tooth so I'll get no caries

indicators.note: treated means worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I'll here supplies just its I

explanation.surface: A dentist reassures that treatment means no decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' says the answer plus SO and I can be rearranged to give NO CARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A crena is a rounded notch or tooth on a crenate margin, such as a leaf edge.

clue.text: Santa's helpers — seamen, might one suppose

definitions.meaning: first sense: reindeer, which pull Santa's sleigh
second sense, playful: the word looks like tar-hands, hands being crew and tars sailors

explanation.walkthrough: The tarand is an old word for reindeer; the second half jokes that the word could name sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarand is an archaic name for the reindeer, the animals that draw Father Christmas's sleigh.

clue.text: What's Þzzing? This, right!

indicators.note: This stands for the answer itself: the clue says the fizzing word equals this plus right, so right must be taken off

parts.note: astir means bustling, in a ferment, so fizzing with activity

explanation.surface: A drinker asks what is bubbling in the glass and is told, yes, this one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as an equation: ASTIR (fizzing) is this answer plus R (right), so removing R leaves it. The whole clue also defines it, as Asti is a sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy, so it is literally something that fizzes.

clue.text: Necklace created in jet or coral

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the necklace's letters run across the end of jet, through or, into the start of coral

explanation.surface: A necklace crafted from jet or coral.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts, a kind of necklace.

clue.text: Second crumpet? Tip on grass

parts.note: a pikelet is a regional British name for a crumpet, a griddle cake

explanation.surface: Asking for another crumpet, with a gardening tip about the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a spongy British griddle cake eaten toasted; pikelet is its Midlands and northern name.
explanation.definitionFit: A spikelet is a small flower spike at the tips of grass stems, the unit of a grass flower head.

clue.text: Introduction to private tip-off from group in Hampstead

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken from within the word that follows

parts.note: the three letters sit in the middle of the word Hampstead

explanation.surface: A private tip whispered by a clique in Hampstead, a well-to-do London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Pst is the hissing sound used to catch someone's attention before a whispered secret.

clue.text: Fires up superstar on the pitch?

definitions.meaning: first sense: to fuel a fire or rouse feelings, a verb in the third person
second sense: Ben ..., the star England cricket all-rounder

explanation.walkthrough: The pitch is the cricket pitch; Ben Stokes is England's famous all-rounder and captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stokes a furnace feeds it fuel, and the cricketer Ben Stokes shares the name.

clue.text: Brownish coin, head effaced after time

indicators.note: head effaced means the first letter is rubbed out, as if worn off the coin

parts.note: a penny is a coin

explanation.surface: A worn copper coin whose head has been rubbed away over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head effaced' rubs out the first letter of PENNY, leaving ENNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenny, or tenné, is the heraldic tincture of orange-brown, a colour.

clue.text: Wrought iron stairs in edges of stairwell, rising spirally one way

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters between the edges
edges of means the first and last letters of stairwell

parts.note: the first and last letters of stairwell

indicators.note: wrought means worked into shape, so the letters are fashioned anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrought-iron staircase spiralling up a stairwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistrorsal describes a spiral that twists to the left as it climbs, like some climbing plants.
